To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the potential soil erosion in Prosecco DOC (215 km2) is 411,000 Mg year-1 (19.5 Mg/ha), with the highest erosion rates (40 Mg/ha) clustered in steep vineyard slopes.

“Soil erosion in Prosecco DOC is 3.3 times higher than the threshold limit defined for Europe, but it could be reduced by 3 times in the completely green scenario, saving about 50 percent of soil in the Proseco DOCG”.
“Soil erosion in vineyards of the Prosecco wine area (NE Italy) can be reduced by 3 times by adopting a green land-management scenario, which is a sustainable solution for the wine industry”.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the potential soil erosion in Prosecco DOC area, in order to support decision-makers in the design of a sustainable wine-production system, with a view to reduce soil loss and to improve soil quality.
the potential soil erosion in a viticultural landscape, by estimating a soil footprint of wine production in the historical Procecco DOCG.

the development of a soil footprint of wine production, by a spatially explicit approach to quantify the impact of agricultural practices on soil erosion, in order to improve the sustainability of viticultural systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Prosecco wine production in NE Italy is currently running at the cost of a soil degradation, which can be effectively reduced by a nature-based approach in agricultural land management.
a green vineyard management could save about 1.2 Mt of soils in the Proseco DOCG every year, which is about 2 times the amount of soil eroded by the whole Veneto Region in 10 years (2008–2018).
soil erosion should be considered as a crucial issue to sustain wine production in the Proseco DOCG, as well as in all other viticultural areas in the Mediterranean Region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a soil erosion reduction of 3.2 times in vineyards, by a 100% grass inter-row cover, could be achieved in the Proseco DOCG area, with a reduction of 1.2 kg soil/bottle of sparkling wine produced.
the Prosecco wine, one of the most famous sparkling wines in the world, has an environmental cost in soil loss, which is 3 times higher than the European soil erosion threshold.

soil erosion in the area is a major threat to the sustainability of the production of sparkling wine, but that the adoption of a sustainable land management can reduce soil erosion to levels that are not detrimental for the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adoption of sustainable agricultural management practices is a necessary step to preserve soil resources and to sustain the future wine production in this area.

the soil erosion rate in the Proseccos DOCG area is high and the adoption of nature-based practices could be an effective tool to mitigate soil erosion, reducing the environmental footprint of wine production.
the adoption of a nature-based approach in viticultural area is crucial, to reduce soil erosion and to preserve soils and landscapes.
